scope: Single-pool desktop physical layout, system and title partition ID queries, and transfers from the title memory budget to the system budget.
receipt: xmem-partitions PASS stable_cpu_pfns=2 budget_reduced=1 ids=2 native_handles=0
reference_behavior: XbGetPartitionHandleAndId accepts partitions 0 (system), 1 (title), 2 (tools). Both outputs are optional. A missing partition sets ERROR_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND. An unknown selector sets ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.
XMemGetPhysicalMemoryLayout writes two 64-bit words. xvcmgmt uses the first 4 KiB page frame number of the title memory ranges. Single-pool topologies repeat the first PFN in the second word.

XMemTransferMemory sends direction 0 from the title to the system memory partition. It rounds the transfer up to a multiple of 512 4 KiB pages. The retail profile rejects directions 1 and 2 when the tools partition is absent.
provider_checks: Presence and ID for selectors 0 and 1, missing tools and invalid selector with output canaries
Two allocated 64 KiB page tokens at the reported title boundary and the next 16-PFN interval, followed by free
Zero-byte transfer, tools gating, invalid direction and overflow rejection
A transfer of 256 MiB minus one byte measurably reduced the working-set budget
limits: Stock Proton has no native memory partition handles. TuxBox reports IDs for desktop memory and leaves both handle and ID outputs untouched when a requested handle is unavailable. The query-only native Windows handle path has not been run on a Windows control. The guest budget is enforced for TuxBox CPU physical pages.
